lane: Backend/AI + mobile: Oracle answers with the model and picks up to two tools; compact chips in the room
goal: Owner 11/11 after the device test: Oracle only gives an on-device canned suggestion (OR-01 decision 31/10, option b) and its large action cards feel heavy. Turn Oracle into a real AI host: ai-oracle-turn calls the oracle_router model route, the model writes a short reply and chooses 0-2 tools from the enabled oracle-actions catalog (draw Tarot, ask a guide, open the Council, astrology, Journal, reflect here) with allowlisted parameters; the server validates them and builds the action cards; the app calls the server when signed in and shows the tools as small one-line chips. This supersedes the 31/10 on-device decision at the Owner's request.
successCriteria: ai-oracle-turn: safety signal answers first (unchanged); then the persona_chat switch, then one shared Chat+Oracle attempt (event persona_message_attempted, limit personaChat.dailyLimit) before any model call; 429 daily_limit_reached and 503 usage_check_unavailable or feature_paused.
The system prompt is the pinned Oracle bundle plus a tool contract; the model returns JSON {reply, tools[]}; the check runs inside the router so a malformed answer tries the fallback model once.

Server keeps only enabled catalog tools, at most two, deduplicated; guide slugs, Council templates, Tarot topics and astrology focus must be in allowlists or fall back to the heuristic handoff; reply at most 700 characters.
When both models fail the function returns 503 oracle_unavailable (the app shows the busy notice); a model safety block returns no tools.
Without model dependencies (tests, local) the handler keeps today's local_fallback response.

App: signed in with a backend, Oracle calls the server with history and nickname consent flags; offline, busy, limit and paused errors show notices like guide chat; offline crisis reply still answers on the device; without a backend the on-device router stays.
OracleRoom shows tools as one-line chips (icon + label), the first one highlighted, detail as accessibility hint; the banner says Oracle is AI when the server answers.
Deno tests for tool parsing and the handler, app tests and tsc pass.
untouchedSurfaces: The pinned Oracle prompt bundle (prompt-composition) is not edited; the tool contract is appended in oracle-tools.ts.
No migration: Oracle uses the persona_chat switch and shares its daily attempts.
Journal memory and birth data are still never sent to Oracle.
Deploying ai-oracle-turn is an Owner action after review.

impact.entryPoint: Nilaza Oracle room from the Chat tab and the floating Oracle button.

impact.backendContract: ai-oracle-turn returns moderationStatus passed with model-chosen actionCards; same response shape the app already reads.
impact.adminVisibility: Pausing guide chat in Admin also pauses Oracle AI; traces appear under feature oracle_router.
impact.privacySafety: Question, up to 12 history turns and nickname (only with the profile flag) go to the provider through OpenRouter with ZDR and data collection denied; crisis replies stay static and free.
impact.observability: Router traces for oracle_router; oracle_turn_created usage metadata records generationStatus and tool kinds.
impact.rollback: Redeploy the previous ai-oracle-turn version (local_fallback) or pause guide chat; the app falls back to notices, not canned answers.

managerTestPath: After the Owner deploys ai-oracle-turn and installs a new APK: open Oracle, tell a short love worry; the reply is AI-written and shows at most two small chips such as 'Trải bài' and 'Hỏi một người dẫn'; tapping a chip opens that feature with the question carried over. A crisis phrase shows 115 and no chips.
residualRisk: Model may pick a weaker tool; tool choice quality needs live QA. Oracle and chat share 5 attempts a day, so heavy Oracle use leaves fewer guide messages.
